p.i: lustres Domini Comites, saepenumero cogitanti, in mentem venire solent, hoc tempore publice exponenda censui. Quod enim mihi propemodum fatale esse videam, a flore Nobilitatis & ingeniosa Iuventutis, huc ad nos accedente, officijs humanitatis exhilarari: mei muneris esse reor, non solum amabilem suavissimorum colloquiorum & beneficiorum usumfructum (quem ad mitigandos leniendosq; dolores meos, quos multis jam annis sustinui, non parum esse efficacem, reipsa expertus sum) magnifa-cere: sed etiam Reipub. gratulari messem copiosam vera Nobilitatis: cui hoc studio est, cum externis illis praesidijs & ornamē-tis veras animi dotes, Timorem Dei, Veritatem, Iusticiam, Temperantiam, Fortitudi-nem, Modestiam, & alias eximias virtutes, prudenter & constanter adiungere. Donec enim iuvenes eiusmodi ingenys & donis praestantes, divinitus excitari, & in theatrum Reipub. Christiana a Deo Opt. Max. produci videro: Catone nostri seculi contentus, bene sperabo de Repub. ut qui non sine propicia Dei providetia hac exi-mia

page.notes: The first word is a fragment ("lustres", printed "lustres", for Illustres) and the page continues a previous one. The first line is printed as a fragment with a swash initial, which I have read as plain "l". The page carries no separate page number. The signature "a 3" is at the foot. "Ꝗuod" is printed with a swash Q, which I have written as "Quod". The word "mia" on the last line completes "exi-mia" and is part of the text. Long s has been written as plain s throughout.
